title.jcr:title: Got questions? We have the answer

question.jcr:title: How do I install ColdFusion?

answer.text: Get help installing ColdFusion. Download the product from the ColdFusion Downloads page.

question.jcr:title: Why won't ColdFusion install?

answer.text: Check the system requirements and ensure your environment meets the minimum specifications.

question.jcr:title: Can I download a trial copy of ColdFusion?

answer.text: Yes, you can download a free 30-day trial from the ColdFusion Downloads page. The trial includes all enterprise features.

question.jcr:title: My trial is expiring soon. How do I convert it?

answer.text: At the end of the 30-day trial period, the Trial edition of ColdFusion automatically becomes the Developer edition, a free, full-featured server for development use only. If you want to build and deploy applications, purchase either ColdFusion Standard or Enterprise edition. Learn more.

question.jcr:title: How do I create my first ColdFusion application?

answer.text: Follow the Getting Started tutorial to create your first CFML page. You only need a text editor and a running ColdFusion server.

question.jcr:title: What are the system requirements?

answer.text: ColdFusion runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Check the system requirements page for detailed hardware and software specifications.

question.jcr:title: Where can I find tutorials?

answer.text: Visit the ColdFusion Learning Center for video tutorials, code samples, and step-by-step guides for beginners and advanced users.

question.jcr:title: How do I connect to a database?

answer.text: Use the ColdFusion Administrator to create a data source. See the database connectivity guide for supported databases and configuration steps.

question.jcr:title: What frameworks work with ColdFusion?

answer.text: Popular frameworks include ColdBox, FW/1, and CFWheels. Each provides MVC architecture and tooling for building scalable applications.

question.jcr:title: How do I deploy a ColdFusion application?

answer.text: Deploy using CAR archives, Docker containers, or manual file copy. Refer to the deployment guide for production best practices.

question.jcr:title: How to debug ColdFusion code?

answer.text: See debug applications using ColdFusion Builder plugin for Visual Studio Code for more information.

question.jcr:title: What is CFML?

answer.text: CFML (ColdFusion Markup Language) is a scripting language for rapid web application development. It integrates seamlessly with HTML and supports both tag-based and script-based syntax.

question.jcr:title: What are the key CFML tags?

answer.text: Key tags include cfquery, cfoutput, cfloop, and cfcomponent. See the CFML reference for the full list.

question.jcr:title: How does CFML differ from other languages?

answer.text: CFML is designed specifically for web development with built-in support for databases, sessions, email, and PDF generation. It abstracts common tasks that require libraries in other languages.

question.jcr:title: Where can I find CFML reference documentation?

answer.text: The complete CFML Reference is available in the official documentation, covering all tags, functions, and objects.

question.jcr:title: How do I update ColdFusion?

answer.text: Use the built-in updater in ColdFusion Administrator or download updates from the Adobe Updates page. Always back up your server before applying updates.

question.jcr:title: What is included in the latest update?

answer.text: Review the release notes for a detailed list of new features, bug fixes, and security patches in each update.

question.jcr:title: How do I check my current ColdFusion version?

answer.text: Open the ColdFusion Administrator and check the System Information page, or use server.coldfusion.productversion in your code.

question.jcr:title: Are updates backward compatible?

answer.text: Most updates are backward compatible. Check the compatibility notes in each release for any breaking changes or deprecated features.
